items.readable_text:
Content:
We can use fraction models to multiply any two fractions.

Content:
Let's figure out how to use models to compute the following product:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{3}{5} \times \dfrac{2}{3}]

Content:
We start with the model of [MATH: \dfrac{3}{5}.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/8658f23cb6ae437311982a1bae016940]

Content:
Since we need to multiply by [MATH: \dfrac{\color{red}2}{\color{blue}3}], we split the whole into [MATH: \color{blue}3] equal parts horizontally. But this time, we keep the shaded pieces in the bottom [MATH: \color{red}2] rows.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/d4c8d9300f65e6c7dffdb971fcf99cc3]

Content:
From the picture on the right, we see that the shaded part represents [MATH: \dfrac{6}{15}] of the whole.

Content:
Therefore,
[MATH: \dfrac{3}{5} \times \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{6}{15}.]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
We can use fraction models to multiply any two fractions.

Content:
Let's figure out how to use models to compute the following product:

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{3}{5} \times \dfrac{2}{3}]

Content:
We start with the model of [MATH: \dfrac{3}{5}.]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/8658f23cb6ae437311982a1bae016940]

Content:
Since we need to multiply by [MATH: \dfrac{\color{red}2}{\color{blue}3}], we split the whole into [MATH: \color{blue}3] equal parts horizontally. But this time, we keep the shaded pieces in the bottom [MATH: \color{red}2] rows.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/d4c8d9300f65e6c7dffdb971fcf99cc3]

Content:
From the picture on the right, we see that the shaded part represents [MATH: \dfrac{6}{15}] of the whole.

Content:
Therefore,
[MATH: \dfrac{3}{5} \times \dfrac{2}{3} = \dfrac{6}{15}.]

---
